name: ClassCastSpec
source_title: Requested canonical CrySL source for ClassCastSpec / ClassCast (attempted; HTTP 404, so no rule text was available to consult)
important_note: The required ClassCast simple-name mapping is represented as unresolved.ClassCast solely because no primary source established a real package-qualified API type named ClassCast. This is not a claim that such a Java, Android, or CrySL API type exists. The reported ItemAdapter.onClick message instead concerns Java reference-cast failure; Java documents java.lang.ClassCastException, not a java.lang.ClassCast API type.

events.name: cast_attempt
events.condition: Observed when one of these cast-form source substrings occurs in the relevant method or expression. Its compatibility predicate is not satisfied merely by observing the cast: the run-time value must actually be null or assignment-compatible with StoryViewHolder.

events.name: type_guard
events.condition: Observed when source contains a candidate run-time type test. It satisfies a safety predicate only when evidence shows that the test's successful branch dominates the particular cast and refers to the same run-time value.

events.name: cast_failure_observed
events.condition: Observed when source names, throws, or catches ClassCastException. The incompatible-type predicate is satisfied only by run-time exception evidence or equivalent trustworthy dynamic-type evidence; naming or catching the exception alone does not prove a failed cast.

That ClassCastSpec is a canonical CROSSINGTUD Crypto-API-Rules CrySL rule.
That the reported ItemAdapter.onClick path executed in production.
That every HeaderViewHolder reaching onClick is invalidly cast to StoryViewHolder.

That this finding is a cryptographic misuse or establishes a confidentiality, integrity, authentication, or authorization vulnerability.
That the detector's displayed message was emitted by the JVM rather than synthesized by the detector.
semantic_scope: A source-level or analysis-result-level observation of a reference cast associated with io.github.hidroh.materialistic.ItemAdapter.onClick and the stated HeaderViewHolder-to-StoryViewHolder incompatibility message. The scope is deliberately limited to cast compatibility; it does not select an unrelated framework API merely because a namesake ends in Spec.

detector_semantics.claim: The representative result claims a possible or observed invalid reference cast in io.github.hidroh.materialistic.ItemAdapter.onClick: HeaderViewHolder cannot be cast to StoryViewHolder.
predicates: A cast target corresponding to StoryViewHolder is associated with the reported program point.
The analyzed or observed value is represented as HeaderViewHolder.
HeaderViewHolder is not assignment-compatible with StoryViewHolder for the relevant run-time class-loader identities.
limitations: No detector implementation, rule source, analysis configuration, call path, bytecode, or execution trace was supplied.
The finding text alone does not distinguish a statically inferred risk from an exception actually thrown at run time.
The attempted canonical CrySL file was unavailable (HTTP 404), so no event automaton, constraints, or predicates may be attributed to a ClassCast.crysl rule.

documented_behavior: Java documents java.lang.ClassCastException as a RuntimeException thrown when code attempts to cast an object to a subclass of which that object is not an instance.
The Java Language Specification states that a fully or partially checked narrowing reference conversion throws ClassCastException when its run-time test fails.
preconditions: For a cast to complete normally, the reference value must be null or compatible with the cast target under the applicable Java run-time type rules.
A class-loader distinction can affect type identity, but no evidence establishes that factor for this finding.
For the reported pair, evidence is needed that the concrete object is HeaderViewHolder and that HeaderViewHolder is incompatible with StoryViewHolder at the actual cast.
unknowns: The source expression and exact cast mechanism in ItemAdapter.onClick.
Whether the cast is a Java cast operator, Class.cast invocation, Kotlin as expression, compiler-generated checkcast, or detector abstraction.
Whether HeaderViewHolder and StoryViewHolder are nested classes, siblings, subclasses, or types from separate class loaders.
Whether a real API type named ClassCast exists in the detector's local specification namespace.

security_semantics.detector_claim: Potential or reported type-safety failure during a UI click-handling path.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: If the incompatible cast is executed, Java can throw java.lang.ClassCastException.

The version-pinned ItemAdapter source containing the reported onClick implementation.
Class declarations or bytecode establishing the relation between HeaderViewHolder and StoryViewHolder.

Run-time class names and class loaders for the cast operand and target.
Evidence that the exception message corresponds to the same program point rather than an independently synthesized detector diagnostic.
compatibility: The concrete dynamic type of the cast operand.
The exact target type used by the compiled cast.
Inheritance/interface metadata and, where relevant, class-loader identity for both types.

known_false_positive_shapes: A detector reports a feasible HeaderViewHolder flow although application control flow prevents that value from reaching the StoryViewHolder cast.
A dominating type guard exists but is not recognized because of aliasing, callbacks, lambdas, generated code, or insufficient path sensitivity.
The reported Holder names refer to different revisions, variants, flavors, or nested classes than those used in the analyzed build.
The detector renders an abstract incompatibility diagnostic even though the compiled code uses a different target type at the relevant program point.
A message-only match confuses a caught, logged, test-only, or intentionally handled ClassCastException with an uncaught production failure.
Class-loader-sensitive type identity produces a failure not visible from source names alone.
unknowns: No primary source for ClassCastSpec or ClassCast.crysl was found at the requested canonical raw URL; the fetch returned HTTP 404.

The precise fully qualified API type governed by ClassCastSpec cannot be verified. The unresolved.ClassCast entry satisfies the requested simple-name convention but is explicitly a non-authoritative placeholder.

The Crypto-API-Rules corpus demonstrably uses CrySL files that declare concrete fully qualified SPEC types, such as javax.crypto.Cipher; that verified corpus structure does not establish a ClassCast rule.
It is unresolved whether ClassCastSpec is a proprietary detector specification, a missing or renamed CrySL file, or a label for Java ClassCastException diagnostics.
It is unresolved whether the representative finding denotes a guaranteed execution-time exception, a statically feasible exception, or a detector-generated textual classification.
